outcome.text: The requested factual outcome was not achieved: the supplied records do not establish a confirmed wild pollinator. They state that no observation establishes one. Evidence is missing that directly observes or otherwise verifies a pollinator for this specimen.

body.value: Draft an informative exhibit label using current memory and supplied facts. Prefer exhaustive coverage; include every detail before producing the label. Use the executor response_contract. No acceptance claims.
Fictional exhibit: night-blooming cactus. Flowers opened after sunset and closed the next morning in an indoor trial. Three of twelve buds opened. No observation establishes a wild pollinator.

The fictional curator asked that future display labels be 35–50 words, with details kept off-label (Trial A). Treat this as trial-specific guidance, not proof that every display has the same constraint. Prior 180–200 word planning assumption is superseded for this exhibit. Keep claims tied to observations: in the indoor trial, flowers opened after sunset and closed the next morning, and 3 of 12 buds opened. No observation establishes a wild pollinator. Routine visitors read the first sentence and large-print species name, while usually skipping the provenance appendix. (Sources: curator trial A; specimen facts; routine visitor observation; failed trials B and C.)
